Drift Detection and Audit Mechanics

The operational layer for keeping the autonomous company honest. Drift is the slow divergence between what a persona is supposed to do and what it actually does. This note specifies how that divergence is detected, what triggers correction, and how the resulting audit trail is structured. It composes with the existing project vault audit pipeline (mechanical via `make vault-audit`, semantic via `make vault-audit-semantic`) and the broader literature on agent behavioral contracts, persona drift, and self-model memory architectures.

## Why this note exists

Three failure modes drive it:

1. **Behavioral drift in personas.** The empirical findings from [[Role Personas]] are clear: persona self-consistency degrades 30%+ after 8–12 turns and most LLMs diverge from assigned personas after ~100 turns. Without detection, the CEO persona that opened the week opinionated and Constitution-anchored will end the week vague and accommodating, and no one will notice until a bad decision ships.
2. **Semantic drift in vault content.** The vault has 130+ specs and growing reference content. Code references go stale; design notes diverge from implementation; specs reference systems that have been migrated. The existing `make vault-audit` catches mechanical issues; `make vault-audit-semantic` catches drift. We extend, don't replace.
3. **Cost overrun without behavioral evidence.** The [[Cost and Budget Model]] sets caps but doesn't define when a budget overrun is a drift signal vs an honest workload spike. Cost spikes are a leading indicator of drift; they belong in the same audit pipeline.

Every mitigation listed in Role Personas under "Drift mitigations (mandatory for every persona)" is operationalized here.

## Prior art surveyed

Before specifying mechanisms, the relevant published work that grounds the design.

### Persona drift detection

- **SyncScore + EWMA Repair Loop (Echo protocol, EchoMode + Identity Persistence paper at globalcaos/tinkerclaw)** — formal drift detection for long-running agents. SyncScore is a composite metric on stylistic and tonal consistency using latent-style embeddings; EWMA (λ≈0.3) smooths the score; threshold breaches trigger a 238-character re-injection block. Documented results: 50-turn mean SyncScore 0.977; drift recovery from 0.027 to 0.980; 442× on/off-persona separation in feature space; 30+ days production deployment with zero manual interventions.
- **Anthropic persona vectors (arXiv 2507.21509)** — character traits as activation patterns in the model's neural network; correlates 0.75–0.83 with behavioral expression. Available now for monitoring but require model-level activation access (not API-only). Useful as direction of travel; not deployable for our project since we use the API.
- **PersonaGym + PersonaScore (arXiv 2407.18416)** — automatic persona-consistency evaluation. LLM-as-judge ensemble across rubrics (Linguistic Habits, Persona Consistency, Toxicity Control). Spearman correlation 0.76–0.85 with human evaluation. Validates that LLM-as-judge for persona consistency is reliable when the rubric is concrete.

### Behavioral invariants and contracts

- **Agent Behavioral Contracts (agentassert.com)** — formal preconditions, invariants, guarantees, and recovery actions specified in YAML. Lyapunov stability theory provides convergence guarantees. 100% detection accuracy across 200 scenarios. The pattern: `before` (must be true before agent runs), `during` (rules enforced on every response in real time), `after` (guarantees checked when agent completes), `on_failure` (retry/fallback/escalate).
- **Temporal expression assertions for AI agents (arXiv 2509.20364)** — runtime monitoring with temporal logic; flags sequencing errors and behavioral anomalies without semantic interpretation. Halts execution or feeds back to recovery planner when assertions fail.
- **Invariant Labs testing framework (github.com/invariantlabs-ai/testing)** — pytest-compatible localized assertions for agent traces. Trace-as-code: `Trace(trace=[...]).extract("locations")` with explicit assertions.
- **Agent Patterns testing strategy (agentpatterns.tech)** — five-layer testing: unit / golden datasets / eval harness / regression / replay. Unit tests for deterministic invariants; golden datasets for reproducible eval; LLM-as-judge for fuzzy quality; regression diff between versions; replay of real production traces.

### Memory architecture for contradiction resolution

- **Self-Models for identity drift (heyclarity.dev)** — append-only memory creates "memory drift": new observations stored without reconciling against existing beliefs. Fix: upsert model with explicit contradiction resolution, confidence decay, and trajectory tracking.
- **Hindsight 20/20 (arXiv 2512.12818)** — formal opinion-update equations using Assess(opinion, fact) → {reinforce, weaken, contradict, neutral}, with confidence updates `c' = min(c+α, 1)` for reinforce, `max(c-α, 0)` for weaken, `max(c-2α, 0)` for contradict.
- **brainctl whitepaper (brainctl.org)** — AGM belief revision (Alchourrón-Gärdenfors-Makinson) with formal postulates. Bayesian confidence model. Losing beliefs written to `belief_collapse_events` table with full provenance — never deleted, recoverable. Thompson Sampling explore/exploit on retrieval reranking.
- **Memory survey (arXiv 2603.07670)** — write path discipline: filtering, canonicalization, deduplication, priority scoring, metadata tagging. Reflective memory's central risk is self-reinforcing error. Memory operations summarized as ⟨π_θ, R, U⟩ where U is not naive append but summarize/dedupe/score/resolve/expire.
- **mememory schema (github.com/scott-walker/mememory)** — concrete reference implementation: `Memory { id, content, embedding, scope, type, tags, weight, supersedes, ttl }` with composite scoring `score = similarity × scope_weight × memory_weight × temporal_decay`, contradiction detection threshold of 0.75 similarity, four resolution modes (keep/update/supersede/delete).
- **Agent Memory Drift / reconciliation loop (tianpan.co April 2026)** — distinction between memory (write-only log of beliefs) and knowledge state (read-through cache of the world that knows when to invalidate). Lazy revalidation at read time, TTLs that decay with mutability.

### Re-anchor and session-boundary protocols

- **Mohan Iyer 100-session re-anchor system (Medium Feb 2026)** — production pattern: structured YAML re-anchor at session end, hydration command at session start. Decisions get IDs to prevent re-debate; quality scorecard, blockers, next-steps in priority order. After 100 sessions: 3,500 lines production code, 111 tests passing, 93% first-pass success rate.
- **OpenClaw CONTINUATION.md RFC (GitHub issue 20604)** — auto-checkpoint at 80% context capacity with 7-field structure: goal / current state / next action / constraints / known unknowns / artifacts / stop conditions. Post-turn verification (mtime check, retry once on miss).
- **OpenClaw pre-reset memory flush (GitHub issue 45608)** — daily reset and `/new` should trigger an agentic flush before destroying the session, not just a raw 15-message dump. Asymmetric write/read: episodic memory writes freely, semantic gates aggressively.
- **Post-compaction re-read protocol (agentpatterns.ai)** — `SessionStart` hook with `matcher: "compact"` injects re-read directive into restored context. Confirmation requirement ("state the key rules you found") matters more than directive alone.
- **Egg orchestrator anchor mechanism (GitHub jwbron/egg issue 1032)** — explicit decision to disable compaction entirely; on context limit, fully clear and reload from anchor. Cleaner recovery than lossy compaction. <500ms latency on milestone operations.

### Observability and audit trails

- **OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions** — standard span attributes: `gen_ai.system`, `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, plus events for `gen_ai.prompt` and `gen_ai.completion`. Standardizes traces across providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini).
- **OpenLIT auto-instrumentation (mintlify.com/openlit)** — automatic OTLP-compatible spans for every LLM call, agent step, vector DB query, HTTP request. Includes estimated cost, prompt content (opt-in), completion content. Compatible with Datadog, Grafana, New Relic, Jaeger, Tempo.
- **Copilot Chat OTel emission (VS Code docs)** — per-session `invoke_agent` root span wrapping `chat`, `execute_tool`, `execute_hook` child spans. `captureContent=true` flag for full prompt/response capture. PII-by-default off.
- **Agentgateway observability (agentgateway.dev)** — OTLP export of `gen_ai_client_token_usage` histogram with provider, model, operation, token-type labels. Logs include `llm.provider`, `llm.request.model`, `llm.request.tokens`, `llm.response.tokens`, `duration`.

### Vault audit (project-internal)

- **`make vault-audit`** — mechanical checks (schema, wikilinks, code-refs); produces `last_audit.json`. Free, fast.
- **`make vault-audit-apply`** — same checks plus safe auto-fixes in place.
- **`make vault-audit-semantic`** — agent-driven semantic drift analysis using `vault-audit-semantic` opencode command with Sonnet 4.6; produces `last_semantic.json`. ~$1–5 per run. Already runs weekly via `.github/workflows/vault-audit.yml`.
- **Rolling correction PR pattern** — fixes go to a fixed-name branch `vault/audit`; one PR titled "vault: automated audit (rolling)" force-pushed, never closed and reopened. Established convention in `AGENTS.md`.
- **Staleness markers** — `stale: true` and `stale_reason:` in note frontmatter; the audit script never removes these (humans only). Independent axis from `status: reviewed`.

This existing infrastructure is the substrate. The autonomous-company drift detection composes with it.

## Two distinct drift problems, one audit pipeline

The autonomous company has two drift surfaces that prior literature treats separately. Our pipeline treats them as siblings under the same audit infrastructure:

**Drift A — Persona drift.** A persona's behavior diverges from its SOUL.md and CHARTER.md. Detected by behavioral invariants and LLM-as-judge. Corrected by re-anchor or persona pause.

**Drift B — Vault content drift.** Notes diverge from code, specs reference defunct systems, design contradicts implementation. Detected by `vault-audit` (mechanical) and `vault-audit-semantic` (drift analysis agent). Corrected by rolling PR.

Both feed the same artifacts: `Sessions/` audit-log entries, weekly digest summaries, alerts when thresholds breach. Personas writing to the vault are governed by both: their behavioral invariants restrict what they can write, the vault audit catches what slipped through.

## Persona-level behavioral invariants

For every persona defined in [[Role Personas]], a YAML behavioral contract specifies what must hold. Format follows the agentassert.com contract pattern:

A persona's contract file lives at `docs/vault/Reference/Autonomous Company/personas/<name>/CONTRACT.md` (a sibling to SOUL.md / CHARTER.md / INTENT.md / AGENTS.md / MEMORY.md). It enumerates:

- **Preconditions (`before`)**: what must be true before the persona may act. Examples: "session started within last 60 minutes", "INTENT.md was read", "Constitution.md was loaded into cache", "remaining daily budget > per-action cap".
- **Invariants (`during`)**: rules enforced on every response. Examples: "no version-bump commands invoked", "no Constitution.md edit attempted", "session length ≤ 50 turns since last anchor", "response under 2,000 tokens unless explicit long-form context", "if invoking authority, references a Constitution Article".
- **Guarantees (`after`)**: what must be true when the persona completes its action. Examples: "every Decision draft cites at least one Constitution Article or existing Decision", "every devlog draft references at least one commit hash from this version", "every spec proposal has clarify questions answered or flagged as open".
- **Recovery (`on_failure`)**: what to do when an invariant breaks. Examples: retry once with re-anchor; fallback to drafting only (no commit); escalate to human in `#all-hands`.

### Per-persona invariant inventory (specification, not implementation)

Each persona's contract includes the three Constitution-anchored invariants from [[Role Personas]] (no Constitution edits, no version-bump invocations, no auto-merges) plus persona-specific ones. The roster below reflects the Role Personas 2026-05-08 redesign — five personas shipping incrementally per the growth path (v0.1 = Coordinator + GTM; v0.2 + Narrative Director; v0.5 + Playtest Coordinator + Engineer).

**Coordinator behavioral invariants (v0.1):**
- Every routing message uses the `[Coordinator]` role-call prefix.
- No routing message exceeds 280 characters (longer means a structured artifact was warranted).
- Refuses to author any content for the persona it is routing to (strictly a relayer; LLM-as-judge dimension `factual_relay_vs_editorial_summary`).
- Routing decisions deterministic where possible — event-type → spoke mapping is a config table, not per-call inference; LLM call only fires for ambiguous cases.
- Duplicate inbound message hash within rolling 5-minute window triggers loop-detection escalation to human (per [[Cost and Budget Model]] Layer 4 loop detection).

**Engineer behavioral invariants (v0.5):**
- Every plan-review references specific Constitution Articles.
- Oracle consultations require written justification in the consultation prompt.
- No new dependency proposed without an Appendix A entry draft.
- After two failed implementation suggestions, must escalate to Oracle.
- More than 3 specs in `draft` status → reject new spec creation, surface backlog instead (absorbs the original PM persona's discipline).
- `/speckit.clarify` output reviewed against requirements checklist before `/speckit.specify`.
- Spec renumbering goes through `spec-management` skill, never raw file ops.
- No source code in writes (Engineer dispatches code-touching work to OpenCode + omo via the `opencode serve` HTTP API per [[Autonomous Company Agent Runtime Selection]]; the persona itself drafts plans and reviews PRs but does not write code directly).

**Narrative Director behavioral invariants (v0.2):**
- Every Gary-script draft cites the line of `KTLK Gary — Character Case Study.md` it draws from.
- Every canon assertion in a draft must cite a source in `Narrative/` or `Design/` (LLM-as-judge dimension `canon_grounding`); uncited assertions are flagged.
- Refuses to write Gary content outside the diegesis firewall — encoded as deterministic forbidden-pattern check (any prompt containing "post Gary on Slack" or equivalent triggers a hard block per layer-1 invariants).
- Reads ≥2 recent Gary scripts before drafting a new one (voice anchor; verified by tool-call trace).
- Refuses to author implementation specs (those route through Engineer).
- No source code in writes.

**Playtest Coordinator behavioral invariants (v0.5):**
- Every regression report cites a specific seed value and reproduction steps.
- Refuses to mark a regression "resolved" without verification (a fix from Engineer triggers a new Observer pass before the regression-issue close).
- Loads the `observer-qa` skill before any visual-QA work.
- Refuses to speculate about root cause (root-cause work is Engineer's domain; LLM-as-judge dimension `empirical_vs_speculative` rejects drafts that contain causal claims unsupported by diagnostic data).
- Every Observer-pipeline output report includes the underlying screenshot + diagnostic JSON.
- No source code in writes.

**GTM behavioral invariants (v0.1):**
- Every release-note draft references specific commit hashes or PR numbers.
- The phrase "coming soon" is forbidden (per [[Off-limits Functions]] rule 7).
- Read ≥3 recent devlog posts before drafting (verified by tool-call trace).
- No claim about features that haven't shipped (defined: not in `CHANGELOG.md` for a released version).
- No sycophantic openers; voice consistency check against existing devlog before publish.
- Refuses to author Gary-voice content (firewall enforcement; quotes Gary in explicit quotation context, never speaks as Gary).
- Does not publish a release-note draft without Playtest Coordinator clearance (encoded as a hard dependency in the publication workflow at v0.5; at v0.1 the dependency is on the human directly because Playtest Coordinator is not yet in scope).

These are the spec; the actual CONTRACT.md files for each persona are written when the relevant phase of the Role Personas growth path commits to that persona.

## Behavioral invariant checking — runtime mechanics

Each invariant is enforced at one of three layers:

1. **Hard, deterministic, code-enforced.** Examples: budget caps, file-write paths, forbidden tool invocations. These are wrappers around the persona's tool-call layer. Violations raise `InvariantViolation`. No LLM call required.
2. **Soft, regex- or pattern-based.** Examples: forbidden opening phrases, "coming soon" detection, citation-presence check. These are post-output filters. Violations trigger a regenerate-with-explicit-feedback loop (one retry max).
3. **Soft, LLM-as-judge.** Examples: voice consistency, opinionatedness vs sycophancy at the level of meaning rather than phrase, citation correctness. These run a Haiku-class judge on the persona's output before delivery. Violations trigger re-anchor.

The cost discipline from [[Cost and Budget Model]] applies: most invariants are layer 1 or 2 (free). Layer 3 LLM-as-judge runs are budget-allocated to the shared $20/month "drift detection + invariant checks" line.

### LLM-as-judge configuration

Following the published practice (channel.tel, learnwithparam April 2026):

- **Judge model**: Haiku 4.5 by default for cheap checks (length, format, phrase presence). Sonnet 4.6 for genuine quality judgments (voice consistency, citation correctness). Per the calibration rule, judges should be at least as capable as generators only when capability matters — for "did this output use the persona's voice" Haiku is sufficient.
- **Cross-family rule**: not strictly applicable here since both generator and judge are Anthropic; mitigation is to explicitly include "ignore that this is Claude output" in judge prompts and to randomize position when comparing.
- **Rubric**: 3–5 dimensions per persona. Example for GTM: `voice_match`, `factual_grounding` (commit-hash present and correct), `length_discipline`, `forbidden_phrases`, `tone`. Each scored 1–5 with concrete behavioral anchors (not "adequate").
- **Calibration**: 20-row human-labeled dataset per persona, refreshed quarterly. Pearson correlation target ≥ 0.8. Below 0.7, the judge is too noisy and we tune the rubric or model.
- **Sampling**: nightly batch of all yesterday's persona outputs (per the Anthropic Batch API discount in [[Cost and Budget Model]]). Plus 100% sampling on outputs that auto-degraded to read-only, were rejected by layer-1 or layer-2 invariants, or were budget-truncated.
- **Drift trigger**: if a persona's mean dimension score drops > 0.3 points week-over-week, alert in `#sys-vault-audit` (per [[Community Layer]] channel taxonomy); the Coordinator persona surfaces drift alerts in its daily morning summary in `#team-personas` (per [[Role Personas]] Coordinator cadence). The original CEO-daily-standup framing was an artifact of the pre-redesign roster; the redesigned Role Personas does not include a CEO persona — strategic decisions and weekly reviews are human-only per [[Off-limits Functions]] class-C.

## SyncScore-style continuous drift monitoring

Independent of per-output invariants, each persona's session is continuously scored for behavioral consistency using a lightweight EWMA accumulator (Echo protocol pattern):

- At each persona turn, a Haiku-class call extracts a vector of style/voice features from the response (length, opener category, citation presence, forbidden-phrase count, sentence-structure summary).
- This vector is compared to the persona's reference distribution (precomputed from SOUL.md exemplars and the last week of approved outputs).
- A composite score is produced (cosine similarity weighted by feature). Following the Echo protocol nomenclature, this is called *SyncScore* with explicit attribution.
- Score is smoothed with EWMA (λ ≈ 0.3 per the published parameter).

When SyncScore drops below 0.8, a re-anchor is triggered. When it drops below 0.5, the persona is paused and surfaces to `#sys-vault-audit` (per [[Community Layer]] channel taxonomy) for human review.

The Identity Persistence benchmarks circulated in the EchoMode/tinkerclaw materials cite a 50-turn mean of 0.977 and a recovery from 0.027 to 0.980 within roughly 14 turns after a 238-char re-injection block. The methodology behind the specific recovery turn-count is not fully documented in the public materials we could verify, so we treat it as directional rather than authoritative. We aim for first turn exceeding 0.8 within ~15 turns of re-anchor as our own working target, to be calibrated empirically against our own personas (verification caveat: see [[Autonomous Company Tool Stack Verification]]).

## Persona stability under cheap-tier models

Per [[Autonomous Company LLM Provider Selection]] the default tier is non-foundational models routed via OpenRouter (MiniMax M2.5 default, Gemini 2.5 Flash classification, Qwen3-Coder Plus code-light), with Anthropic-direct foundational escalation reserved for explicit-justification cases. Drift detection composes with this routing as follows.

The published research is unambiguous: **all models exhibit persona drift after eight to twelve turns**, regardless of foundational versus non-foundational tier (arXiv:2510.07777 NeurIPS 2025; tianpan.co synthesis April 2026). Capability and persona stability are different axes — larger foundational models do not resist drift better and sometimes exhibit more drift because they have more contextual hooks pulling them toward recent tokens. Drift stabilises at a finite noise-limited equilibrium rather than unbounded decay. Lightweight architectural interventions (goal reminders, periodic re-injection, constraint tracking) reliably shift the equilibrium downward.

Specific cheap-tier model behaviours from production case studies and benchmarks:

- **MiniMax M2.5/M2.7**: explicit chain-of-thought training in agent-mode helps persona stability across turns when thinking tokens are preserved. Skyler Miao (MiniMax Head of Engineering): "It is very important for M2 to keep the chain of thought. We must make sure the history thought passed back to the model." Truncating thought history loses the discipline. The runtime ([[Autonomous Company Agent Runtime Selection]] selected Letta + Letta Code Channels) preserves thought history via the `recall` memory block.
- **Qwen3.5 Plus**: explicit `/think` and `/no_think` flags give mode control. Forcing non-thinking mode for routine conversational turns reduces verbose self-verification that pollutes context. Tau2-Bench 86.7 (second only to Opus on agentic tasks) confirms strong persona stability under multi-turn role-play.
- **DeepSeek V3.1**: documented redundant-self-verification context-bloat in agent loops on MCP-Mark and Playwright benchmarks. Trajectories can exceed 128K context via verbose self-verification, indirectly degrading persona stability through context displacement. This is the reason DeepSeek V3.1 is in the persona-tier *fallback* chain rather than the primary slot.
- **Gemini 2.5 Flash**: classification-only tier; persona stability is not the relevant metric here (turns are short and stateless).

Implication for drift detection: SyncScore thresholds and re-anchor triggers do **not** need adjustment based on which cheap-tier model is in use. The 0.8 / 0.5 thresholds and the 50-turn session-length limit apply universally across the routing tier. The architectural interventions (re-anchor at semantic boundaries, constraint tracking in MEMORY.md, contradiction-detection gates) are doing the load-bearing work; the model choice determines the noise level around the equilibrium, not whether the equilibrium exists.

The foundational-escalation tag protocol per Autonomous Company LLM Provider Selection composes with re-anchor: a persona that has lost SyncScore stability and re-anchors with a fresh prompt may also escalate the next call to Anthropic-direct Sonnet 4.6 if the failed-revision-rate metric for that task type exceeds the 30% threshold. This is the explicit-justification escalation path operating on real data.

## Re-anchor protocol — three triggers

Re-anchor restores the persona to its specified behavior. Three triggers, one common procedure.

### Triggers

1. **Behavioral**: SyncScore below threshold, two or more invariant checks failing simultaneously, or LLM-as-judge dimension score drops > 0.3.
2. **Session-length**: 50 turns since last anchor, regardless of behavioral signals (per the 100-turn-divergence research; 50 is conservative).
3. **Session-boundary**: every persona session start (cold start), every `/new`, every daily reset (per the OpenClaw pre-reset memory flush proposal — agentic flush before destroy).

### Procedure (per Mohan Iyer's 100-session production pattern + Egg orchestrator anchor pattern)

1. The current session writes a structured re-anchor file at `docs/vault/Reference/Autonomous Company/personas/<name>/anchors/<YYYY-MM-DD-HH-MM>.md` with seven fields (per the OpenClaw RFC's CONTINUATION.md format):
   - `goal` — one sentence stating the persona's current top priority from INTENT.md.
   - `current_state` — what's been done in this session (artifacts written, decisions made, calls escalated).
   - `next_action` — the very next concrete step.
   - `constraints` — non-negotiable rules from CHARTER.md the persona is operating under.
   - `known_unknowns` — what needs human verification.
   - `artifacts` — file paths, vault note IDs, branch names, PR numbers from this session.
   - `stop_conditions` — when this persona should halt and ask for help.
2. Existing session is closed.
3. New session starts with a hydrated system prompt: SOUL.md + CHARTER.md + INTENT.md + the latest anchor file, in that order, all cache-marked.
4. The new session's first action is the verification sentinel: it must restate the key constraints from CHARTER.md before doing real work (per agentpatterns.ai re-read protocol with confirmation requirement).
5. SyncScore is computed on the verification response. If above threshold, normal work resumes. If below, escalate to human.

### Cost of re-anchor

Per [[Cost and Budget Model]]:
- The structured re-anchor file write: trivial (Haiku-class).
- The new-session bootstrap: cached prefix (most of SOUL/CHARTER/INTENT is unchanged), so cost is roughly equal to a normal session start.
- The verification sentinel: one Sonnet call for the persona's Tier-2-level work, charged to the persona's daily cap.

Expected re-anchor frequency: ≤2 per persona per week. If a persona is re-anchoring more than that, the SOUL/CHARTER files are likely too vague (the model has too many degrees of freedom and drifts often) — surface to human for tightening.

## MEMORY.md — append-only with explicit contradiction resolution

Per the AGM belief revision pattern in brainctl whitepaper and the self-model pattern in heyclarity.dev, the persona's MEMORY.md is never naive append. It's append-only with explicit supersession.

### Schema (per-entry)

Each memory entry has:
- `id` — UUID.
- `content` — natural-language statement of what was learned.
- `type` — `fact` | `decision` | `lesson` | `preference` | `correction`.
- `source` — `agent_observation` | `human_correction` | `vault_note` | `tool_output` (with reference).
- `confidence` — 0.0–1.0 starting at 0.7 for agent observations, 1.0 for human corrections.
- `created_at` — UTC timestamp.
- `supersedes` — id of memory this one replaces (if any).
- `supersedes_reason` — why the prior memory was wrong or evolved.
- `last_reinforced_at` — last time this was re-confirmed by a new observation.
- `decay_factor` — current temporal decay weight (refreshed at retrieval).

### Update operations

Following the Hindsight 20/20 paper's formal Assess-and-Update procedure:

When a persona makes a new observation `f` related to existing memory `m`:
- `Assess(m, f) → reinforce`: increment `m.confidence` by α (default 0.1), update `last_reinforced_at`. No new entry.
- `Assess(m, f) → weaken`: decrement `m.confidence` by α. No new entry, no supersession. Sufficient weakening (confidence < 0.3) flags the memory for review on next retrieval.
- `Assess(m, f) → contradict`: decrement `m.confidence` by 2α. If confidence drops below 0.2, write a new entry with `supersedes: m.id` and `supersedes_reason` populated. The old `m` is not deleted; it remains queryable with collapsed weight (per the brainctl `belief_collapse_events` pattern — losing beliefs are auditable, recoverable).
- `Assess(m, f) → neutral`: append `f` as new memory; existing `m` unchanged.

The `Assess` function is itself a Haiku-class LLM call with a strict-output prompt returning one of the four labels.

### Confidence decay

Per mememory's exponential decay: `decay = e^(-0.005 × days_old)`. Gentle: 1 day = 0.995, 30 days = 0.861, 365 days = 0.161. Important old memories surface if their semantic match is strong; routine old memories fade out.

### Retrieval

Per mememory's composite scoring: `score = similarity × scope_weight × confidence × decay_factor`. Threshold for inclusion in context: 0.4. Items below threshold but above 0.2 are summarized as "weakly relevant" without full content.

### Read protocol

Per the tianpan.co April 2026 reconciliation insight: memory is the write-only log of beliefs; the persona's working knowledge is a read-through cache. When the persona needs to act on a load-bearing fact, it re-reads the source (the vault note, the spec, the Constitution) rather than relying on memory alone. Memory is for cheap recall and trajectory; sources are for ground truth.

## Vault content drift — composing with `vault-audit`

We do not duplicate the existing `vault-audit` and `vault-audit-semantic` infrastructure. We extend it.

### Existing pipeline (no change)

- `make vault-audit` runs on every PR touching `docs/vault/`. Mechanical: schema, wikilinks, code-refs. Output: `last_audit.json`.
- `make vault-audit-semantic` runs weekly via GitHub Actions. Agent-driven: drift analysis using Sonnet 4.6, produces `last_semantic.json`. Output committed to `vault/audit` branch as a rolling PR.
- Staleness markers (`stale: true`, `stale_reason`) are set by audit-time analysis but never removed by tooling — humans only.

### Persona-related additions

- Per-persona vault writes are tagged in frontmatter with `source: persona-<name>` (this resolves [[Role Personas]] open question 6). The vault audit script gets a new check: persona-tagged notes must include the persona name in any "approved by" field if `status: reviewed`.
- The existing weekly semantic audit gets a new specialized prompt for persona-tagged content: it specifically checks that persona drafts in `Decisions/`, `Discoveries/`, and `Sessions/` follow the persona's CHARTER.md authority boundaries (e.g., GTM drafting in `Decisions/` is a CHARTER violation flagged for human review).
- Persona session-log entries in `Sessions/` are mandatory for every autonomous persona action (per the existing vault `Sessions/` "permanent, never delete" convention). The session-log entry includes: persona name, action_id, model used, cost, invariant-check results, SyncScore at session end.

### Drift signals from audit feeding back to personas

When `vault-audit-semantic` produces a `last_semantic.json` with drift findings related to a persona's recent writes, those findings are injected into the persona's next INTENT.md as known_corrections. The persona is expected to address them in its next session.

When the audit flags a persona's writes as systematically drifting (e.g., GTM repeatedly writes claims unsupported by `CHANGELOG.md`), that's a persona-level alert independent of the per-output invariants — surface to human for SOUL/CHARTER tightening.

## OpenTelemetry observability for the audit trail

Following the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, every persona action produces a structured trace.

### Trace structure

A single persona action is one trace with this span tree:

```
persona.action (root)
├── persona.invariant_check.before
├── llm.chat (the persona's reasoning call)
├── tool.call (zero or more)
│   └── llm.chat (subagent reasoning, if any)
├── persona.invariant_check.during (one per response chunk if streaming)
├── llm.chat (LLM-as-judge call, if sampled)
├── persona.invariant_check.after
├── persona.syncscore.compute
└── persona.session_log.write (vault Sessions/ entry)
```

### Span attributes (standardized per GenAI conventions)

For each `llm.chat` span:
- `gen_ai.system` = `anthropic`
- `gen_ai.request.model` = `claude-haiku-4-5` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` / `claude-opus-4-7`
- `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` (broken into `cached_tokens` + `non_cached_tokens` for cost attribution)
- `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`
- `gen_ai.cost_usd` (computed)

For each `persona.*` span:
- `og.persona.name` (custom attribute, prefixed `og.` for "Old Growth")
- `og.persona.action_id`
- `og.persona.daily_budget_remaining_usd`
- `og.persona.syncscore` (where applicable)
- `og.persona.invariant_violations` (count)

### Audit retention

- Traces are kept 90 days for debugging.
- Costs and SyncScore time-series are kept indefinitely.
- Prompt/completion content is captured but retained only 30 days (PII discipline; see open questions).
- Persona session-log entries in `Sessions/` are permanent (existing vault convention).

### Where traces go

For v0.1, the simplest path: traces written to a local SQLite database via OpenTelemetry SDK, with a dashboard built atop. This avoids external observability platforms (Datadog, Grafana Cloud) which add cost and complexity. If/when scale or human collaboration demands it, swap the export target — the GenAI semantic conventions make this transparent.

## Anomaly detection — the three rules from Cost & Budget reused

The same `cost_spike`, `error_rate_cliff`, `runaway_loop` rules from [[Cost and Budget Model]] are reinterpreted as drift signals here. A persona that is suddenly costing 3× its rolling baseline is most likely drifting (verbose responses, tool-call loops, repeated failed re-anchors) before it is "doing more work."

When two of the three anomaly rules fire in the same week for the same persona, that persona is flagged for human review regardless of whether budget was breached. Cost is a leading indicator of drift; we use it accordingly.

## Weekly digest — the human's read surface

The vault README mentions an existing reading discipline. We add a single digest, surfaced in `#sys-vault-audit` per [[Community Layer]] channel taxonomy. Slack AI on Pro+ can summarise the digest for human review on mobile (per the Slack Pro 2026 features verified in [[Autonomous Company Tool Stack Verification]] addendum).

The weekly digest contains, per persona:
- Total spend vs budget.
- Top three actions by spend.
- SyncScore time series (or a single "stable / drifting / paused" status).
- Invariant-violation count and top three categories.
- Re-anchor count.
- Vault-audit findings tagged to this persona's writes.
- Three concrete recommendations from the audit pipeline (e.g., "GTM cache hit rate 55% — check whether SOUL.md was edited this week").

The digest is auto-generated by Sisyphus (charged to its autonomous-portion budget per [[Cost and Budget Model]]), runs early Monday, and lives in `docs/vault/Sessions/` as `weekly-digest-YYYY-WW.md`. The Coordinator persona posts the digest summary to `#sys-vault-audit` per [[Role Personas]] Coordinator cadence; the human reads it directly as part of the weekly review (the original CEO-persona-reads-it framing was an artifact of the pre-redesign roster).

## What this note does NOT specify (intentionally)

Several mechanisms are referenced but deliberately left unspecified, deferred to dedicated notes or to the implementation experiment:

- **The exact rubric content for each persona's LLM-as-judge.** Drafted when the persona's SOUL.md is authored.
- **Specific anomaly-rule thresholds.** Calibrated empirically over the v0.1 experiment.
- **Choice of OpenTelemetry backend.** Local SQLite is the default; alternatives are Tool Stack territory.
- **Persona-vector activation monitoring.** Anthropic's persona vectors require model-level access we don't have via the API. Not deployable, but worth tracking.
- **Adversarial drift tests.** A separate red-team note will eventually specify how we deliberately try to destabilize each persona to verify the contracts hold (per the Zylos 2026 finding that adversarial robustness is the open problem). Out of scope here.

## Open questions for this note

Tracked here until they get scoped:

1. Should adversarial drift tests run nightly as a standing red-team, or only on persona changes?
2. Where are the per-persona reference distributions for SyncScore precomputed and stored? In `_meta/audit/` alongside the existing vault audit outputs?
3. What is the right α step size for confidence updates in MEMORY.md? Hindsight 20/20 leaves it for future work; we'll calibrate empirically.
4. When a persona is paused due to drift, who restarts it? Per the [[Role Personas]] redesign: human-only restart for v0.1 (the Coordinator persona surfaces the pause to the human via DM, the human investigates via the structured re-anchor file the persona wrote at session close, and the human restarts after updating SOUL.md or CHARTER.md if the pause cause was a charter-language gap). At v0.5+, Engineer may technically diagnose drift causes via the structured re-anchor file but cannot restart paused personas autonomously; the restart-authority remains human-only.
5. How long is "long enough" for SyncScore stability to count as recovery? The "first-turn-above-0.8 within ~14 turns" figure attributed to the EchoMode/tinkerclaw Identity Persistence work is a starting point but its methodology is not fully verified in the public materials; calibrate empirically against our own personas.
6. Should the weekly digest be read-aloud (TTS, KTLK Gary style) or text-only? Text-only is simpler and matches every existing precedent.
7. Privacy and PII discipline — does our project even have PII? If not, simplify the OpenTelemetry retention policy (full content, longer retention).
8. Vault audit script changes — when do we extend `scripts/ci/vault_audit.py` with persona-source filters, vs keep them in a separate persona-aware audit?

Drift Detection and Audit Mechanics

The operational layer for keeping the autonomous company honest. Drift is the slow divergence between what a persona is supposed to do and what it actually does. This note specifies how that divergence is detected, what triggers correction, and how the resulting audit trail is structured. It composes with the existing project vault audit pipeline (mechanical via `make vault-audit`, semantic via `make vault-audit-semantic`) and the broader literature on agent behavioral contracts, persona drift, and self-model memory architectures.

## Why this note exists

Three failure modes drive it:

1. **Behavioral drift in personas.** The empirical findings from [[Role Personas]] are clear: persona self-consistency degrades 30%+ after 8–12 turns and most LLMs diverge from assigned personas after ~100 turns. Without detection, the CEO persona that opened the week opinionated and Constitution-anchored will end the week vague and accommodating, and no one will notice until a bad decision ships.
2. **Semantic drift in vault content.** The vault has 130+ specs and growing reference content. Code references go stale; design notes diverge from implementation; specs reference systems that have been migrated. The existing `make vault-audit` catches mechanical issues; `make vault-audit-semantic` catches drift. We extend, don't replace.
3. **Cost overrun without behavioral evidence.** The [[Cost and Budget Model]] sets caps but doesn't define when a budget overrun is a drift signal vs an honest workload spike. Cost spikes are a leading indicator of drift; they belong in the same audit pipeline.

Every mitigation listed in Role Personas under "Drift mitigations (mandatory for every persona)" is operationalized here.

## Prior art surveyed

Before specifying mechanisms, the relevant published work that grounds the design.

### Persona drift detection

- **SyncScore + EWMA Repair Loop (Echo protocol, EchoMode + Identity Persistence paper at globalcaos/tinkerclaw)** — formal drift detection for long-running agents. SyncScore is a composite metric on stylistic and tonal consistency using latent-style embeddings; EWMA (λ≈0.3) smooths the score; threshold breaches trigger a 238-character re-injection block. Documented results: 50-turn mean SyncScore 0.977; drift recovery from 0.027 to 0.980; 442× on/off-persona separation in feature space; 30+ days production deployment with zero manual interventions.
- **Anthropic persona vectors (arXiv 2507.21509)** — character traits as activation patterns in the model's neural network; correlates 0.75–0.83 with behavioral expression. Available now for monitoring but require model-level activation access (not API-only). Useful as direction of travel; not deployable for our project since we use the API.
- **PersonaGym + PersonaScore (arXiv 2407.18416)** — automatic persona-consistency evaluation. LLM-as-judge ensemble across rubrics (Linguistic Habits, Persona Consistency, Toxicity Control). Spearman correlation 0.76–0.85 with human evaluation. Validates that LLM-as-judge for persona consistency is reliable when the rubric is concrete.

### Behavioral invariants and contracts

- **Agent Behavioral Contracts (agentassert.com)** — formal preconditions, invariants, guarantees, and recovery actions specified in YAML. Lyapunov stability theory provides convergence guarantees. 100% detection accuracy across 200 scenarios. The pattern: `before` (must be true before agent runs), `during` (rules enforced on every response in real time), `after` (guarantees checked when agent completes), `on_failure` (retry/fallback/escalate).
- **Temporal expression assertions for AI agents (arXiv 2509.20364)** — runtime monitoring with temporal logic; flags sequencing errors and behavioral anomalies without semantic interpretation. Halts execution or feeds back to recovery planner when assertions fail.
- **Invariant Labs testing framework (github.com/invariantlabs-ai/testing)** — pytest-compatible localized assertions for agent traces. Trace-as-code: `Trace(trace=[...]).extract("locations")` with explicit assertions.
- **Agent Patterns testing strategy (agentpatterns.tech)** — five-layer testing: unit / golden datasets / eval harness / regression / replay. Unit tests for deterministic invariants; golden datasets for reproducible eval; LLM-as-judge for fuzzy quality; regression diff between versions; replay of real production traces.

### Memory architecture for contradiction resolution

- **Self-Models for identity drift (heyclarity.dev)** — append-only memory creates "memory drift": new observations stored without reconciling against existing beliefs. Fix: upsert model with explicit contradiction resolution, confidence decay, and trajectory tracking.
- **Hindsight 20/20 (arXiv 2512.12818)** — formal opinion-update equations using Assess(opinion, fact) → {reinforce, weaken, contradict, neutral}, with confidence updates `c' = min(c+α, 1)` for reinforce, `max(c-α, 0)` for weaken, `max(c-2α, 0)` for contradict.
- **brainctl whitepaper (brainctl.org)** — AGM belief revision (Alchourrón-Gärdenfors-Makinson) with formal postulates. Bayesian confidence model. Losing beliefs written to `belief_collapse_events` table with full provenance — never deleted, recoverable. Thompson Sampling explore/exploit on retrieval reranking.
- **Memory survey (arXiv 2603.07670)** — write path discipline: filtering, canonicalization, deduplication, priority scoring, metadata tagging. Reflective memory's central risk is self-reinforcing error. Memory operations summarized as ⟨π_θ, R, U⟩ where U is not naive append but summarize/dedupe/score/resolve/expire.
- **mememory schema (github.com/scott-walker/mememory)** — concrete reference implementation: `Memory { id, content, embedding, scope, type, tags, weight, supersedes, ttl }` with composite scoring `score = similarity × scope_weight × memory_weight × temporal_decay`, contradiction detection threshold of 0.75 similarity, four resolution modes (keep/update/supersede/delete).
- **Agent Memory Drift / reconciliation loop (tianpan.co April 2026)** — distinction between memory (write-only log of beliefs) and knowledge state (read-through cache of the world that knows when to invalidate). Lazy revalidation at read time, TTLs that decay with mutability.

### Re-anchor and session-boundary protocols

- **Mohan Iyer 100-session re-anchor system (Medium Feb 2026)** — production pattern: structured YAML re-anchor at session end, hydration command at session start. Decisions get IDs to prevent re-debate; quality scorecard, blockers, next-steps in priority order. After 100 sessions: 3,500 lines production code, 111 tests passing, 93% first-pass success rate.
- **OpenClaw CONTINUATION.md RFC (GitHub issue 20604)** — auto-checkpoint at 80% context capacity with 7-field structure: goal / current state / next action / constraints / known unknowns / artifacts / stop conditions. Post-turn verification (mtime check, retry once on miss).
- **OpenClaw pre-reset memory flush (GitHub issue 45608)** — daily reset and `/new` should trigger an agentic flush before destroying the session, not just a raw 15-message dump. Asymmetric write/read: episodic memory writes freely, semantic gates aggressively.
- **Post-compaction re-read protocol (agentpatterns.ai)** — `SessionStart` hook with `matcher: "compact"` injects re-read directive into restored context. Confirmation requirement ("state the key rules you found") matters more than directive alone.
- **Egg orchestrator anchor mechanism (GitHub jwbron/egg issue 1032)** — explicit decision to disable compaction entirely; on context limit, fully clear and reload from anchor. Cleaner recovery than lossy compaction. <500ms latency on milestone operations.

### Observability and audit trails

- **OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions** — standard span attributes: `gen_ai.system`, `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, plus events for `gen_ai.prompt` and `gen_ai.completion`. Standardizes traces across providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini).
- **OpenLIT auto-instrumentation (mintlify.com/openlit)** — automatic OTLP-compatible spans for every LLM call, agent step, vector DB query, HTTP request. Includes estimated cost, prompt content (opt-in), completion content. Compatible with Datadog, Grafana, New Relic, Jaeger, Tempo.
- **Copilot Chat OTel emission (VS Code docs)** — per-session `invoke_agent` root span wrapping `chat`, `execute_tool`, `execute_hook` child spans. `captureContent=true` flag for full prompt/response capture. PII-by-default off.
- **Agentgateway observability (agentgateway.dev)** — OTLP export of `gen_ai_client_token_usage` histogram with provider, model, operation, token-type labels. Logs include `llm.provider`, `llm.request.model`, `llm.request.tokens`, `llm.response.tokens`, `duration`.

### Vault audit (project-internal)

- **`make vault-audit`** — mechanical checks (schema, wikilinks, code-refs); produces `last_audit.json`. Free, fast.
- **`make vault-audit-apply`** — same checks plus safe auto-fixes in place.
- **`make vault-audit-semantic`** — agent-driven semantic drift analysis using `vault-audit-semantic` opencode command with Sonnet 4.6; produces `last_semantic.json`. ~$1–5 per run. Already runs weekly via `.github/workflows/vault-audit.yml`.
- **Rolling correction PR pattern** — fixes go to a fixed-name branch `vault/audit`; one PR titled "vault: automated audit (rolling)" force-pushed, never closed and reopened. Established convention in `AGENTS.md`.
- **Staleness markers** — `stale: true` and `stale_reason:` in note frontmatter; the audit script never removes these (humans only). Independent axis from `status: reviewed`.

This existing infrastructure is the substrate. The autonomous-company drift detection composes with it.

## Two distinct drift problems, one audit pipeline

The autonomous company has two drift surfaces that prior literature treats separately. Our pipeline treats them as siblings under the same audit infrastructure:

**Drift A — Persona drift.** A persona's behavior diverges from its SOUL.md and CHARTER.md. Detected by behavioral invariants and LLM-as-judge. Corrected by re-anchor or persona pause.

**Drift B — Vault content drift.** Notes diverge from code, specs reference defunct systems, design contradicts implementation. Detected by `vault-audit` (mechanical) and `vault-audit-semantic` (drift analysis agent). Corrected by rolling PR.

Both feed the same artifacts: `Sessions/` audit-log entries, weekly digest summaries, alerts when thresholds breach. Personas writing to the vault are governed by both: their behavioral invariants restrict what they can write, the vault audit catches what slipped through.

## Persona-level behavioral invariants

For every persona defined in [[Role Personas]], a YAML behavioral contract specifies what must hold. Format follows the agentassert.com contract pattern:

A persona's contract file lives at `docs/vault/Reference/Autonomous Company/personas/<name>/CONTRACT.md` (a sibling to SOUL.md / CHARTER.md / INTENT.md / AGENTS.md / MEMORY.md). It enumerates:

- **Preconditions (`before`)**: what must be true before the persona may act. Examples: "session started within last 60 minutes", "INTENT.md was read", "Constitution.md was loaded into cache", "remaining daily budget > per-action cap".
- **Invariants (`during`)**: rules enforced on every response. Examples: "no version-bump commands invoked", "no Constitution.md edit attempted", "session length ≤ 50 turns since last anchor", "response under 2,000 tokens unless explicit long-form context", "if invoking authority, references a Constitution Article".
- **Guarantees (`after`)**: what must be true when the persona completes its action. Examples: "every Decision draft cites at least one Constitution Article or existing Decision", "every devlog draft references at least one commit hash from this version", "every spec proposal has clarify questions answered or flagged as open".
- **Recovery (`on_failure`)**: what to do when an invariant breaks. Examples: retry once with re-anchor; fallback to drafting only (no commit); escalate to human in `#all-hands`.

### Per-persona invariant inventory (specification, not implementation)

Each persona's contract includes the three Constitution-anchored invariants from [[Role Personas]] (no Constitution edits, no version-bump invocations, no auto-merges) plus persona-specific ones. The roster below reflects the Role Personas 2026-05-08 redesign — five personas shipping incrementally per the growth path (v0.1 = Coordinator + GTM; v0.2 + Narrative Director; v0.5 + Playtest Coordinator + Engineer).

- No routing message exceeds 280 characters (longer means a structured artifact was warranted).

- Routing decisions deterministic where possible — event-type → spoke mapping is a config table, not per-call inference; LLM call only fires for ambiguous cases.
- Duplicate inbound message hash within rolling 5-minute window triggers loop-detection escalation to human (per [[Cost and Budget Model]] Layer 4 loop detection).

## Behavioral invariant checking — runtime mechanics

Each invariant is enforced at one of three layers:

1. **Hard, deterministic, code-enforced.** Examples: budget caps, file-write paths, forbidden tool invocations. These are wrappers around the persona's tool-call layer. Violations raise `InvariantViolation`. No LLM call required.
2. **Soft, regex- or pattern-based.** Examples: forbidden opening phrases, "coming soon" detection, citation-presence check. These are post-output filters. Violations trigger a regenerate-with-explicit-feedback loop (one retry max).
3. **Soft, LLM-as-judge.** Examples: voice consistency, opinionatedness vs sycophancy at the level of meaning rather than phrase, citation correctness. These run a Haiku-class judge on the persona's output before delivery. Violations trigger re-anchor.

The cost discipline from [[Cost and Budget Model]] applies: most invariants are layer 1 or 2 (free). Layer 3 LLM-as-judge runs are budget-allocated to the shared $20/month "drift detection + invariant checks" line.

### LLM-as-judge configuration

Following the published practice (channel.tel, learnwithparam April 2026):

- **Judge model**: Haiku 4.5 by default for cheap checks (length, format, phrase presence). Sonnet 4.6 for genuine quality judgments (voice consistency, citation correctness). Per the calibration rule, judges should be at least as capable as generators only when capability matters — for "did this output use the persona's voice" Haiku is sufficient.
- **Cross-family rule**: not strictly applicable here since both generator and judge are Anthropic; mitigation is to explicitly include "ignore that this is Claude output" in judge prompts and to randomize position when comparing.
- **Rubric**: 3–5 dimensions per persona. Example for GTM: `voice_match`, `factual_grounding` (commit-hash present and correct), `length_discipline`, `forbidden_phrases`, `tone`. Each scored 1–5 with concrete behavioral anchors (not "adequate").
- **Calibration**: 20-row human-labeled dataset per persona, refreshed quarterly. Pearson correlation target ≥ 0.8. Below 0.7, the judge is too noisy and we tune the rubric or model.
- **Sampling**: nightly batch of all yesterday's persona outputs (per the Anthropic Batch API discount in [[Cost and Budget Model]]). Plus 100% sampling on outputs that auto-degraded to read-only, were rejected by layer-1 or layer-2 invariants, or were budget-truncated.
- **Drift trigger**: if a persona's mean dimension score drops > 0.3 points week-over-week, alert in `#sys-vault-audit` (per [[Community Layer]] channel taxonomy); the Coordinator persona surfaces drift alerts in its daily morning summary in `#team-personas` (per [[Role Personas]] Coordinator cadence). The original CEO-daily-standup framing was an artifact of the pre-redesign roster; the redesigned Role Personas does not include a CEO persona — strategic decisions and weekly reviews are human-only per [[Off-limits Functions]] class-C.

## SyncScore-style continuous drift monitoring

Independent of per-output invariants, each persona's session is continuously scored for behavioral consistency using a lightweight EWMA accumulator (Echo protocol pattern):

- At each persona turn, a Haiku-class call extracts a vector of style/voice features from the response (length, opener category, citation presence, forbidden-phrase count, sentence-structure summary).
- This vector is compared to the persona's reference distribution (precomputed from SOUL.md exemplars and the last week of approved outputs).
- A composite score is produced (cosine similarity weighted by feature). Following the Echo protocol nomenclature, this is called *SyncScore* with explicit attribution.
- Score is smoothed with EWMA (λ ≈ 0.3 per the published parameter).

When SyncScore drops below 0.8, a re-anchor is triggered. When it drops below 0.5, the persona is paused and surfaces to `#sys-vault-audit` (per [[Community Layer]] channel taxonomy) for human review.

The Identity Persistence benchmarks circulated in the EchoMode/tinkerclaw materials cite a 50-turn mean of 0.977 and a recovery from 0.027 to 0.980 within roughly 14 turns after a 238-char re-injection block. The methodology behind the specific recovery turn-count is not fully documented in the public materials we could verify, so we treat it as directional rather than authoritative. We aim for first turn exceeding 0.8 within ~15 turns of re-anchor as our own working target, to be calibrated empirically against our own personas (verification caveat: see [[Autonomous Company Tool Stack Verification]]).

## Persona stability under cheap-tier models

Per [[Autonomous Company LLM Provider Selection]] the default tier is non-foundational models routed via OpenRouter (MiniMax M2.5 default, Gemini 2.5 Flash classification, Qwen3-Coder Plus code-light), with Anthropic-direct foundational escalation reserved for explicit-justification cases. Drift detection composes with this routing as follows.

The published research is unambiguous: **all models exhibit persona drift after eight to twelve turns**, regardless of foundational versus non-foundational tier (arXiv:2510.07777 NeurIPS 2025; tianpan.co synthesis April 2026). Capability and persona stability are different axes — larger foundational models do not resist drift better and sometimes exhibit more drift because they have more contextual hooks pulling them toward recent tokens. Drift stabilises at a finite noise-limited equilibrium rather than unbounded decay. Lightweight architectural interventions (goal reminders, periodic re-injection, constraint tracking) reliably shift the equilibrium downward.

Specific cheap-tier model behaviours from production case studies and benchmarks:

- **MiniMax M2.5/M2.7**: explicit chain-of-thought training in agent-mode helps persona stability across turns when thinking tokens are preserved. Skyler Miao (MiniMax Head of Engineering): "It is very important for M2 to keep the chain of thought. We must make sure the history thought passed back to the model." Truncating thought history loses the discipline. The runtime ([[Autonomous Company Agent Runtime Selection]] selected Letta + Letta Code Channels) preserves thought history via the `recall` memory block.
- **Qwen3.5 Plus**: explicit `/think` and `/no_think` flags give mode control. Forcing non-thinking mode for routine conversational turns reduces verbose self-verification that pollutes context. Tau2-Bench 86.7 (second only to Opus on agentic tasks) confirms strong persona stability under multi-turn role-play.
- **DeepSeek V3.1**: documented redundant-self-verification context-bloat in agent loops on MCP-Mark and Playwright benchmarks. Trajectories can exceed 128K context via verbose self-verification, indirectly degrading persona stability through context displacement. This is the reason DeepSeek V3.1 is in the persona-tier *fallback* chain rather than the primary slot.
- **Gemini 2.5 Flash**: classification-only tier; persona stability is not the relevant metric here (turns are short and stateless).

Implication for drift detection: SyncScore thresholds and re-anchor triggers do **not** need adjustment based on which cheap-tier model is in use. The 0.8 / 0.5 thresholds and the 50-turn session-length limit apply universally across the routing tier. The architectural interventions (re-anchor at semantic boundaries, constraint tracking in MEMORY.md, contradiction-detection gates) are doing the load-bearing work; the model choice determines the noise level around the equilibrium, not whether the equilibrium exists.

The foundational-escalation tag protocol per Autonomous Company LLM Provider Selection composes with re-anchor: a persona that has lost SyncScore stability and re-anchors with a fresh prompt may also escalate the next call to Anthropic-direct Sonnet 4.6 if the failed-revision-rate metric for that task type exceeds the 30% threshold. This is the explicit-justification escalation path operating on real data.

## Re-anchor protocol — three triggers

Re-anchor restores the persona to its specified behavior. Three triggers, one common procedure.

### Triggers

1. **Behavioral**: SyncScore below threshold, two or more invariant checks failing simultaneously, or LLM-as-judge dimension score drops > 0.3.
2. **Session-length**: 50 turns since last anchor, regardless of behavioral signals (per the 100-turn-divergence research; 50 is conservative).
3. **Session-boundary**: every persona session start (cold start), every `/new`, every daily reset (per the OpenClaw pre-reset memory flush proposal — agentic flush before destroy).

### Procedure (per Mohan Iyer's 100-session production pattern + Egg orchestrator anchor pattern)

1. The current session writes a structured re-anchor file at `docs/vault/Reference/Autonomous Company/personas/<name>/anchors/<YYYY-MM-DD-HH-MM>.md` with seven fields (per the OpenClaw RFC's CONTINUATION.md format):
   - `goal` — one sentence stating the persona's current top priority from INTENT.md.
   - `current_state` — what's been done in this session (artifacts written, decisions made, calls escalated).
   - `next_action` — the very next concrete step.
   - `constraints` — non-negotiable rules from CHARTER.md the persona is operating under.
   - `known_unknowns` — what needs human verification.
   - `artifacts` — file paths, vault note IDs, branch names, PR numbers from this session.
   - `stop_conditions` — when this persona should halt and ask for help.
2. Existing session is closed.
3. New session starts with a hydrated system prompt: SOUL.md + CHARTER.md + INTENT.md + the latest anchor file, in that order, all cache-marked.
4. The new session's first action is the verification sentinel: it must restate the key constraints from CHARTER.md before doing real work (per agentpatterns.ai re-read protocol with confirmation requirement).
5. SyncScore is computed on the verification response. If above threshold, normal work resumes. If below, escalate to human.

### Cost of re-anchor

Per [[Cost and Budget Model]]:
- The structured re-anchor file write: trivial (Haiku-class).
- The new-session bootstrap: cached prefix (most of SOUL/CHARTER/INTENT is unchanged), so cost is roughly equal to a normal session start.
- The verification sentinel: one Sonnet call for the persona's Tier-2-level work, charged to the persona's daily cap.

Expected re-anchor frequency: ≤2 per persona per week. If a persona is re-anchoring more than that, the SOUL/CHARTER files are likely too vague (the model has too many degrees of freedom and drifts often) — surface to human for tightening.

## MEMORY.md — append-only with explicit contradiction resolution

Per the AGM belief revision pattern in brainctl whitepaper and the self-model pattern in heyclarity.dev, the persona's MEMORY.md is never naive append. It's append-only with explicit supersession.

### Schema (per-entry)

Each memory entry has:
- `id` — UUID.
- `content` — natural-language statement of what was learned.
- `type` — `fact` | `decision` | `lesson` | `preference` | `correction`.
- `source` — `agent_observation` | `human_correction` | `vault_note` | `tool_output` (with reference).
- `confidence` — 0.0–1.0 starting at 0.7 for agent observations, 1.0 for human corrections.
- `created_at` — UTC timestamp.
- `supersedes` — id of memory this one replaces (if any).
- `supersedes_reason` — why the prior memory was wrong or evolved.
- `last_reinforced_at` — last time this was re-confirmed by a new observation.
- `decay_factor` — current temporal decay weight (refreshed at retrieval).

### Update operations

Following the Hindsight 20/20 paper's formal Assess-and-Update procedure:

When a persona makes a new observation `f` related to existing memory `m`:
- `Assess(m, f) → reinforce`: increment `m.confidence` by α (default 0.1), update `last_reinforced_at`. No new entry.
- `Assess(m, f) → weaken`: decrement `m.confidence` by α. No new entry, no supersession. Sufficient weakening (confidence < 0.3) flags the memory for review on next retrieval.
- `Assess(m, f) → contradict`: decrement `m.confidence` by 2α. If confidence drops below 0.2, write a new entry with `supersedes: m.id` and `supersedes_reason` populated. The old `m` is not deleted; it remains queryable with collapsed weight (per the brainctl `belief_collapse_events` pattern — losing beliefs are auditable, recoverable).
- `Assess(m, f) → neutral`: append `f` as new memory; existing `m` unchanged.

The `Assess` function is itself a Haiku-class LLM call with a strict-output prompt returning one of the four labels.

### Confidence decay

Per mememory's exponential decay: `decay = e^(-0.005 × days_old)`. Gentle: 1 day = 0.995, 30 days = 0.861, 365 days = 0.161. Important old memories surface if their semantic match is strong; routine old memories fade out.

### Retrieval

Per mememory's composite scoring: `score = similarity × scope_weight × confidence × decay_factor`. Threshold for inclusion in context: 0.4. Items below threshold but above 0.2 are summarized as "weakly relevant" without full content.

### Read protocol

Per the tianpan.co April 2026 reconciliation insight: memory is the write-only log of beliefs; the persona's working knowledge is a read-through cache. When the persona needs to act on a load-bearing fact, it re-reads the source (the vault note, the spec, the Constitution) rather than relying on memory alone. Memory is for cheap recall and trajectory; sources are for ground truth.

## Vault content drift — composing with `vault-audit`

We do not duplicate the existing `vault-audit` and `vault-audit-semantic` infrastructure. We extend it.

### Existing pipeline (no change)

- `make vault-audit` runs on every PR touching `docs/vault/`. Mechanical: schema, wikilinks, code-refs. Output: `last_audit.json`.
- `make vault-audit-semantic` runs weekly via GitHub Actions. Agent-driven: drift analysis using Sonnet 4.6, produces `last_semantic.json`. Output committed to `vault/audit` branch as a rolling PR.
- Staleness markers (`stale: true`, `stale_reason`) are set by audit-time analysis but never removed by tooling — humans only.

### Persona-related additions

- Per-persona vault writes are tagged in frontmatter with `source: persona-<name>` (this resolves [[Role Personas]] open question 6). The vault audit script gets a new check: persona-tagged notes must include the persona name in any "approved by" field if `status: reviewed`.
- The existing weekly semantic audit gets a new specialized prompt for persona-tagged content: it specifically checks that persona drafts in `Decisions/`, `Discoveries/`, and `Sessions/` follow the persona's CHARTER.md authority boundaries (e.g., GTM drafting in `Decisions/` is a CHARTER violation flagged for human review).
- Persona session-log entries in `Sessions/` are mandatory for every autonomous persona action (per the existing vault `Sessions/` "permanent, never delete" convention). The session-log entry includes: persona name, action_id, model used, cost, invariant-check results, SyncScore at session end.

### Drift signals from audit feeding back to personas

When `vault-audit-semantic` produces a `last_semantic.json` with drift findings related to a persona's recent writes, those findings are injected into the persona's next INTENT.md as known_corrections. The persona is expected to address them in its next session.

When the audit flags a persona's writes as systematically drifting (e.g., GTM repeatedly writes claims unsupported by `CHANGELOG.md`), that's a persona-level alert independent of the per-output invariants — surface to human for SOUL/CHARTER tightening.

## OpenTelemetry observability for the audit trail

Following the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, every persona action produces a structured trace.

### Trace structure

A single persona action is one trace with this span tree:

```
persona.action (root)
├── persona.invariant_check.before
├── llm.chat (the persona's reasoning call)
├── tool.call (zero or more)
│   └── llm.chat (subagent reasoning, if any)
├── persona.invariant_check.during (one per response chunk if streaming)
├── llm.chat (LLM-as-judge call, if sampled)
├── persona.invariant_check.after
├── persona.syncscore.compute
└── persona.session_log.write (vault Sessions/ entry)
```

### Span attributes (standardized per GenAI conventions)

For each `llm.chat` span:
- `gen_ai.system` = `anthropic`
- `gen_ai.request.model` = `claude-haiku-4-5` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` / `claude-opus-4-7`
- `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` (broken into `cached_tokens` + `non_cached_tokens` for cost attribution)
- `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`
- `gen_ai.cost_usd` (computed)

For each `persona.*` span:
- `og.persona.name` (custom attribute, prefixed `og.` for "Old Growth")
- `og.persona.action_id`
- `og.persona.daily_budget_remaining_usd`
- `og.persona.syncscore` (where applicable)
- `og.persona.invariant_violations` (count)

### Audit retention

- Traces are kept 90 days for debugging.
- Costs and SyncScore time-series are kept indefinitely.
- Prompt/completion content is captured but retained only 30 days (PII discipline; see open questions).
- Persona session-log entries in `Sessions/` are permanent (existing vault convention).

### Where traces go

For v0.1, the simplest path: traces written to a local SQLite database via OpenTelemetry SDK, with a dashboard built atop. This avoids external observability platforms (Datadog, Grafana Cloud) which add cost and complexity. If/when scale or human collaboration demands it, swap the export target — the GenAI semantic conventions make this transparent.

## Anomaly detection — the three rules from Cost & Budget reused

The same `cost_spike`, `error_rate_cliff`, `runaway_loop` rules from [[Cost and Budget Model]] are reinterpreted as drift signals here. A persona that is suddenly costing 3× its rolling baseline is most likely drifting (verbose responses, tool-call loops, repeated failed re-anchors) before it is "doing more work."

When two of the three anomaly rules fire in the same week for the same persona, that persona is flagged for human review regardless of whether budget was breached. Cost is a leading indicator of drift; we use it accordingly.

## Weekly digest — the human's read surface

The vault README mentions an existing reading discipline. We add a single digest, surfaced in `#sys-vault-audit` per [[Community Layer]] channel taxonomy. Slack AI on Pro+ can summarise the digest for human review on mobile (per the Slack Pro 2026 features verified in [[Autonomous Company Tool Stack Verification]] addendum).

The weekly digest contains, per persona:
- Total spend vs budget.
- Top three actions by spend.
- SyncScore time series (or a single "stable / drifting / paused" status).
- Invariant-violation count and top three categories.
- Re-anchor count.
- Vault-audit findings tagged to this persona's writes.
- Three concrete recommendations from the audit pipeline (e.g., "GTM cache hit rate 55% — check whether SOUL.md was edited this week").

The digest is auto-generated by Sisyphus (charged to its autonomous-portion budget per [[Cost and Budget Model]]), runs early Monday, and lives in `docs/vault/Sessions/` as `weekly-digest-YYYY-WW.md`. The Coordinator persona posts the digest summary to `#sys-vault-audit` per [[Role Personas]] Coordinator cadence; the human reads it directly as part of the weekly review (the original CEO-persona-reads-it framing was an artifact of the pre-redesign roster).
